findings.evidence: Finite arithmetic example in interfaces.json: pre-witness=0 us, breakpoint=1000 us, dispatch=15000 us, effective resume/stop=50000 us. Dispatch-based elapsed=15000 us passes 20000 us, while actual hold=49000 us does not. This is not a runtime test.
findings.problem: Lines 182-184 describe the selected-hold bound as a pre-instruction witness to release/kill dispatch interval. Dispatch alone is not necessarily the end of a ptrace hold: transport, syscall, signal delivery or scheduling can postpone effective continuation/termination. The stricter pre/post conservative-enclosing-bound requirement at lines 190-196 is sound, but the more specific dispatch wording could be implemented as an undercount.
findings.recommendation: In the prepared target/oracle/receipt contract, use the conservative actual-end bound required by lines 190-196: a post-continuation witness (or demonstrated effective-release upper bound) for resume and independently confirmed target stop/exit for kill, with clock uncertainty included. Retain dispatch as a separate timestamp. Consider a closed validator timing vector where dispatch is timely but effective completion is late or absent; reject the timing claim. If overhead is only conservatively upper-bounded, label it as a bound rather than a measured slowdown.
findings.title: Make the hold-duration endpoint explicit in the executable packet
findings.why_not_a_documentation_blocker: The package already mandates conservative target pre/post witnesses, independent actual-stop evidence and separate review of the exact executable packet. Those requirements admit a safe implementation without changing the design direction or accepting runtime feasibility. This review does not authorize any dispatch-only timing claim.

limitations: This was static/design review, not Docker/image preparation, a runtime test, a capability grant, normative approval or M4 acceptance.

No Docker calls, network acquisition, container/Redis/target-ELF execution, tracing, fault injection, observer implementation or delegated subagents were used. Only review scripts/reports were written, inside the authorized correctness directory.

The original researcher/generator scripts were read but never imported, compiled with exec, or run. Lua was neither run nor compiled. Verification scripts are source/hash/ELF parsers, arithmetic checks and report writers, not observers or runtime validators.
Historical complete post-patch source/toolchain/generated-header/dependency provenance and reproducible binary build remain unproven. Retained upstream byte equality is not that proof.

Independent ELF checking shares pyelftools 0.32 and capstone 5.0.3 with the research; manual ELF/branch/PLT bitfield calculations add independence, not a second full disassembler. No live memory/register/ASLR, hardware-stop precision or optimized VM dataflow claim.
No valid maximum-shape fixture, allocation/memory/expiry headroom, actual argc/argument digest, AOF interval, client transport closure, storage durability or restart oracle was exercised.
The finite timing counterexample is a mathematical design probe, not measured Linux scheduling, a fault-injection control, or a future validator implementation.

Detailed authority/ACL/amendment threat review belongs to the separate security reviewer. This review checked relevant lifecycle correctness and receipt/claim interfaces, not the entire security audit.

Parent cancellation AST-invariance claims were not independently recomputed against the separate cancellation snapshot. Baseline executor functions were independently inspected and AST-hashed; no cancellation source or review was reopened or modified.
